title: Transfer of closed torsion cohomology rigidity to the topological weak Serre hull
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite commutative ring $A$ killed by a power of $\ell$. Let $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E\}$, with discrete topology on $A$ and the induced $\ell$-adic topology otherwise [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Its condensed ring is $P\mapsto C(P,\Lambda)$ on profinite sets.
Let $t:T_0\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Use the small sites and universe of [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Assume that for every torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf] and every integer $q\geq0$, the canonical restriction is bijective:
$$H^q(T_{\mathrm{et}},F)\longrightarrow H^q((T_0)_{\mathrm{et}},t_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}F).$$
Torsion is local torsion, without a common annihilator. These are ordinary right-derived global sections [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] and the actual cohomology pullback [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. Put $\Lambda_V=p_V^*\Lambda$ for $V=T,T_0$, with ordinary uncompleted module-object derived categories [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Let $\mathcal P_T$ be the intersection of all replete classes of $\Lambda_T$-modules containing zero and all finite constant scalar-model constructible modules [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and closed under kernels and cokernels of morphisms between members, extensions, and all small ambient coproducts. In a short exact sequence membership of both ends is sufficient for membership of the middle. For every $M\in\mathcal P_T$, the canonical derived restriction induced by exact module inverse image is an isomorphism in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$:
$$R\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},M[0])\longrightarrow R\Gamma((T_0)_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},t^*M[0]).$$
No henselian base, proper morphism, finite presentation, Noetherianity, invertibility of $\ell$, or completeness of $M$ is assumed. Empty schemes are included.

proof.text: Let $\rho$ be the actual closed restriction transformation, and let $\mathcal E$ be the class of derived objects on which it is invertible. The closed restriction operations theorem supplies additive triangulated functors, shift compatibility and morphisms of distinguished triangles with components exactly $\rho$. Consequently $\mathcal E$ contains zero and is closed under isomorphisms, shifts and triangle extensions. For a retract $K\xrightarrow{i}L\xrightarrow{p}K$, $ip=1_K$, an inverse on $K$ is $\Psi(i)\rho_L^{-1}\Phi(p)$, written in diagrammatic composition order; naturality proves both inverse identities.

proof.text: The normalized product comparison from the operations theorem makes $\mathcal E$ closed under ordinary derived products. For a strict filtered diagram of complexes with one termwise lower bound, take its normalized representatives. Invertibility on the components means the representative comparison maps are quasi-isomorphisms. Exact filtered colimits in abelian groups preserve those quasi-isomorphisms; the cocone equations identify their colimit comparison with $\rho$ on the colimit object. Thus $\mathcal E$ has precisely the infinite-operation closure clauses of an admissible supported image generation class.

Together with the preceding closure properties, this proves that $\mathcal E$ is one of the classes intersected in the supported derived generation hull.
